studies.label: Writer experiment: short-story writing with optional GPT-4 story ideas, rated by separate evaluators

arms.name: Human-only
arms.description: Write a story with no mention of or access to generative AI. The analyzed arm count is not printed (PDF pp. 2, 7).

arms.name: Human with one GenAI idea
arms.description: Option to request one three-sentence story idea from GPT-4 through a fixed prompt; the idea cannot be copied and pasted. The analyzed count is printed in Results (PDF p. 2); intervention details are on PDF p. 7.

arms.name: Human with five GenAI ideas
arms.description: Option to request up to five three-sentence story ideas from GPT-4 through fixed prompts; all requested ideas remain visible and cannot be copied and pasted. The analyzed count is printed in Results (PDF p. 2); intervention details are on PDF p. 7.

studies.task: Write an English story of exactly eight sentences on a randomly assigned adventure topic (open seas, jungle, or another planet) for a teenage and young adult audience.

ai_tool.name: OpenAI GPT-4 via OpenAI's GPT API
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 7, Writer study and experimental conditions; model release year is not stated

preregistration.primary_outcome: Evaluator-rated novelty and usefulness indices; the main text identifies these as preregistered indices and describes tests of the combined AI conditions and the separate AI conditions against Human-only (PDF pp. 2, 8).

open_items: The separately published Supplementary Materials (sections S1-S9, tables S1-S18, figures S1-S6) are not in the saved PDF or markdown. A second local copy contains only the main article. Publisher and Dryad retrieval attempts with the specified User-Agent both failed with WinError 10013 (network/socket access forbidden). Supplementary numerical results and the preregistration could not be checked.

The total randomized count and randomized counts by arm are not printed. The number who began the study is not a randomized count. The paper excludes non-completers and Human-only writers who admitted AI use; the timing and arm allocation of all dropouts are not provided (PDF p. 7).
The Human-only analyzed count and pairwise analyzed participant totals are not printed. They are left null; no counts are derived by arithmetic. The combined-AI analyzed count is also left null.

Outcome SDs, numerical SEs, and numerical confidence intervals are absent from the main PDF. The available arm means are incomplete. In particular, both levels of the across-people similarity outcome are missing; its printed control range is not an SD or an arm mean.

Evaluator-rated results cluster SEs by evaluator rather than writer. A writer-level analysis or uncertainty accounting for repeated ratings of each randomized writer is needed for pooling under codebook section 10. The rating code flags this limitation; it does not claim that the paper treated every rating as independent.

Combined-AI novelty and usefulness effects are stated qualitatively on PDF p. 2 and referred to supplementary section S4. Individual index components and several one-idea emotional-characteristic contrasts have only unlabeled plotted estimates. Their numerical fields remain null.

The main text names GPT-4 but does not state its release year, a dated model snapshot, or the OpenAI embedding model. ai_tool.year is null rather than inferred from outside knowledge or the ethics-approval identifier.

Primary/preregistered status of the similarity measures and individual component items is not confirmed without the preregistration. The five-versus-one usefulness contrast uses a preregistered outcome, but preregistration of that specific contrast is not confirmed.

For the anchoring outcome, PDF p. 5 says that a comparison AI idea is assigned within story topic, whereas PDF p. 8 describes assignment from the same condition. The exact sampling pool cannot be settled from the main article.

PDF p. 2 describes statistically significant preregistered-index differences as coming from the five-idea arm, while PDF p. 3 prints statistically significant one-idea p-values. The numerical results are transcribed as printed; the missing supplement may explain this wording.
notes: Extraction completed 2026-10-09 from the entire markdown conversion, including references and the publisher information page, with methods read before the results and all cited PDF pages independently extracted with pymupdf. No appendices are embedded in this PDF. This is one writer RCT; the separate evaluator sample supplies ratings and is not a second randomized-AI study. All reported full-sample outcome/arm contrasts are retained, including figure-only and qualitative combined-AI records with null effect fields. Figures are not digitized, and no missing effects, SDs, SEs, counts, or means are calculated. Supplementary fixed-effect variants are referred to only qualitatively in the main text and are not separate arm contrasts. Printed percentage changes are retained as paper_effect type other in percentage units; they are not standardized effects. n_units refers to the full analysis reported by the paper, while n_total refers to the two sides of each contrast and is null unless that total is explicitly available. Both AI arms share the same Human-only group, and combined-AI records reuse those participants. AI access was optional; the paper calls its comparison intention-to-treat with respect to idea take-up (PDF p. 6), but it drops some assigned writers (PDF p. 7). The screening form reports no known shared sample. The former screening anchoring outcome is restored under the extraction rules, which impose no outcome cap.
